steps.content: He watches you enter, a composed smile crossing his face.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Long time no see, Chief ${PlayerName}. You always look so grim when you visit me. Rough day at work again?

It's been months since you last saw him, and Adelaide is still wearing bandages. Whether that's because his weak body heals slowly, or because his sharp tongue has earned him another beating from someone else, you can't say.
Though you've heard both the 9th Agency and EDGE have been keeping him under the tightest security, holding him in an isolated cell for over half a year now.
Then again, maybe he's faking it. Or maybe that's just a Fraser thing. Maybe they enjoy being bound up like that over there.
In any case, you sit down across from him and cut straight to the point.
A perfectly measured look of surprise crosses Adelaide's face.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Then I'm very glad you made it back alive.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I know you have deep ties with Sillage. Euphoria was an intelligence hub the two of you founded together. You had dealings at the Great Expo. And during the Ash Campaign, you helped funnel a significant portion of capital to Fraser.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: There's no point in dancing around this. Here's what I want to know: her detailed background, her abilities, her current location, and the sorcery she uses for shifting and hiding between dimensions.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You've been imprisoned here all this time, but the Underground has never sent any rescue. They've abandoned you. There's no need to remain loyal to them anymore.
He chuckles.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: The Campbells are no longer useful to the Underground, just as Fraser is no longer useful to Sillage. I've served my purpose, Chief. If I were in their shoes, I wouldn't risk my neck trying to save a spent pawn either.
His usual spiel again. Despite his huge investment and precarious position, he still tries to sound indifferent, as if he hasn't staked his own life on this gamble.
You pause briefly, then continue.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I believe what you said, that you've achieved your goal. I imagine you're quite confident that the enterprise you've built is already on the right track.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: You must have already placed it in the hands of the <color=#fb9259>right person</color>, haven't you? I may have a chance to invite her here. Your sister, Quinn's President, whose real name is <color=#fb9259>Eirene Campbell</color>.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Or perhaps the one far away in Fraser...
Good. The look on his face right now pleases you.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Hella's quite fond of that young scholar, and DisCity is very interested in Aurum Secretum technology right now. Even with our strained relations with Fraser, I believe it's still possible to invite her to DisCity under the premise of academic exchange.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Oh, I forgot to ask. Which sister would you prefer to see, Mr. Adelaide Campbell?
Adelaide looks at you. For the first time, those heterochromatic eyes lose their composure as he stares directly at you.
Before you can decipher the meaning behind that look, he averts his gaze and lets out a sigh.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: You've picked up some terrible habits lately. You're becoming quite difficult to deal with.

options: I'll keep learning from you in the future.

steps.content: The jab earns you a faint smile from him. Now, the Sage of the Underground straightens up and speaks solemnly, his gaze fixed on you.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: We are the ones who forged a direct pact with the lord of the Underground. Four people. Four flowers. I received her power and sowed her seeds in her stead, so that more worthy souls might be chosen. Since we preach the "gospel of Mania," we might as well call ourselves the <color=#fb9259>Sages</color>.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Pestilence</color>, the plague, dwells in the city's shadows. This Sage seeks out companions through information networks and cognitive influence. She prefers to stay in the shadows, yet she is diligent and reliable in her work... until you "defeated" her. After she "disappeared," DisCity's dark web dissolved along with her.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: <color=#fb9259>Famine</color> embodies the despair of deprivation. Those with nothing left can only turn their gaze toward the very calamity destroying them, borrowing the power of Ash Crystals in exchange for the faintest glimmer of hope. Even among the Sages, this one is the weakest.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I'm not a Sinner. I can only control a few <color=#fb9259>borrowed</color> Apostles, nothing more.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: To the Sage of <color=#fb9259>War</color>, Rancor is the ultimate weapon painstakingly forged by the Underground, yet it was taken by your people so early on. At this point, I'm afraid I know far less about it than that general behind you.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: As for the sage of <color=#fb9259>Death</color>...
His eyes darken for a moment.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: ..She embodies both death and life itself. Be careful, Chief.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: That Sage isn't dangerous because of who she is. Far too many desire her. Her influence has seeped into the world for far too long. You want to take on the abyss, yet you know nothing about it.
...She's death, but also life itself?
[Flashback N9CG back turned] 0.5s

The question rises to your lips, but never leaves them. An inexplicable premonition settles over you, as though you're no longer in the safety of a prison cell under your control, but have been dragged into his domain instead.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: You said the Undergrounders never tried to rescue me. That they've abandoned me... No. I'm the one who told my friends not to make any rash moves.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: It took quite a bit of effort to convince them. I told them not to worry, that DisCity wouldn't kill me. EDGE understands that only by keeping me alive and in captivity can Famine's mark remain in "human" hands. But if I were to die...

He raises his left hand. His face gradually blurs, yet the twisted mark on the side of his palm grows ever clearer—sharp, ominous, shaped like a flower. And with it comes a strange yet familiar feeling.
You think of that woman. Is it her? Wait... It's not that simple.

You feel a resonance of the shackles deep within your soul. Adelaide's voice sounds distant, yet also seems to echo directly within you through some unknown medium. The mark on his hand looks strikingly familiar.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: This power would immediately return to its true owner, then be granted to the next candidate. A new Sage of Famine would be born, becoming a threat to DisCity all over again. And unlike what happened with the Sage of War, you could no longer steal <color=#fb9259>her</color> power.
Adelaide looks at you for a long moment. Then, he smiles.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: You see? Even after meeting your enemy, you still know nothing about her.
The flower dims and fades. He lowers his hand. In an instant, all senses return to normal. Before you sits the same bandaged prisoner, slumped weakly in the familiar, secure confines of the cell.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: I shouldn't say any more. For one thing, my own understanding is limited. And for another, they did help make my wish come true. In any case, they're "friends" I should cherish and be grateful for. As for you...
He looks at you, still smiling, but there's an unsettling earnestness in the smile.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Your "enemy" isn't responsible for every evil in this world, ${PlayerName}. The spread of Mania isn't the result of some kind of conspiracy. It's the echo of our times, what the people want... It was always inevitable.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: All these disasters and tragedies, all this ugliness and absurdity, they were bound to happen, with or without us. The Underground simply glimpsed the inevitable future early on, and resolved to embrace that fate. That's all... They're more determined than anyone else.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Perhaps one day, when your path finally becomes clear to you... you'll become one of them. You'll come to see that enmity was never the only possibility.
He's still smiling. The faint sincerity dissipates entirely, and Adelaide deftly sidesteps your question.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: One last piece of advice: Don't focus only on external threats. You may be surprised to discover that the real danger facing BR-003 and those scientist friends of yours is actually lurking within your own walls.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Advice? Or misdirection? I'm not going to believe everything you say.
He doesn't seem bothered by your response.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: My sister has come so far. She must have received help from many along the way. I can't thank all of them individually, so I'll take this opportunity to thank you in particular. Besides, sharing this information with you hardly changes anything in the grand scheme of things.

steps.speaker: Adelaide
steps.content: Time is running short, Chief. I hope you and your allies are prepared for what's coming.
Then the man falls silent, and you know the interrogation is over. The realization astonishes you. It's as if you began to understand him at some point. As if he no longer feels like an enemy.

...Was it the flower? From the moment he revealed it, a dangerous sense of familiarity began creeping through your nerves—like a warm greeting, or an ominous warning: Something is drawing closer and closer to you.
Don't let it come closer.
You stand up abruptly, grab your coat, and head for the door.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: ...If I need to, I'll be back.
[Black screen] Door closing sound, 1s
The meeting doesn't sway you from your original plan. Using BR-003 as bait to lure out the Underground proves successful, and the Observation Hub soon welcomes its "honored guests" once more.

steps.speaker: Evelleon
steps.content: If this is what he wants...
steps.female_content: If this is what she wants...
